result.instructions: Tools for Tamigo, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "Which departments do we have in Tamigo, and what are their keys?"; "Show planned vs worked hours per employee for last week."; "Who is absent next week and is it approved?". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes Tamigo data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run tamigo_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run tamigo_request_feature to record the request. Paid plan: Pro (unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month), $9/month or $90/year). Pro can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run tamigo_upgrade (plan "monthly" or "yearly"); it returns a payment link for the user to open. tamigo_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: tamigo_list_departments
tools.title: List departments
tools.description: List all departments (shops, restaurants, units) of the company: DepartmentId (a GUID, used by other tools), DepartmentKey (the POS key set in Tamigo), Name, IsDefault and ParentDepartmentId. GET /departments/application/.

include_parents.description: Also return the parent (grouping) departments, not only the leaf units. Default false.

offset.description: Skip this many items (default 0). Pass the previous reply's next_offset.

limit.description: Items to return, 1-1000 (default 200). The reply's next_offset says where to continue.

tools.name: tamigo_list_employees
tools.title: List employees
tools.description: List all employees of the company (basic): EmployeeId, Name, Email, IsPlanner, PosKey (the employee key used by the attendance tool) and DepartmentRoles. For contract, wage and absence-balance details use tamigo_list_employee_details. GET /employees/.

offset.description: Skip this many items (default 0). Pass the previous reply's next_offset.

limit.description: Items to return, 1-1000 (default 200). The reply's next_offset says where to continue.

tools.name: tamigo_list_employee_details
tools.title: List employee details
tools.description: Detailed employee records, 500 per page in alphabetical order: contact data, roles per department, home department, contract hours, wage type and history, absence balances, competencies, custom columns, notes and availability. Bank details and ID numbers are never returned. Large pages are returned in slices: pass the reply's next_page and next_offset to continue. GET /employees/getemployeedetails/.

page.description: Page number, from 0 (default 0). Pass the previous reply's next_page.

include_deleted.description: Also include deleted employees. Default false.

offset.description: Skip this many employees within the page (default 0). Pass the previous reply's next_offset.

limit.description: Items to return, 1-500 (default 50). The reply's next_offset says where to continue.

tools.name: tamigo_list_shifts
tools.title: List shifts (original, planned, worked)
tools.description: Per employee and day, the original rota, the planned (current) rota and the worked (timesheet) hours for a date range, with department, employee POS key, email and wage number. Use it for payroll checks, hours worked vs planned and who worked when. Shift values are hours. GET /shifts/all/{start}/{end}/.

department_id.description: Department id from tamigo_list_departments. Omit for all departments.

offset.description: Skip this many items (default 0). Pass the previous reply's next_offset.

limit.description: Items to return, 1-1000 (default 200). The reply's next_offset says where to continue.

tools.name: tamigo_list_absences
tools.title: List absences
tools.description: All absences (holiday, sickness, leave) that overlap a date range: employee, department, absence type, start and end, and whether it is approved or rejected. GET /LeaveRequests/All/.

offset.description: Skip this many items (default 0). Pass the previous reply's next_offset.

limit.description: Items to return, 1-1000 (default 200). The reply's next_offset says where to continue.

tools.name: tamigo_get_opening_hours
tools.title: Get opening hours
tools.description: Normal and special opening hours per department for a date range. GET /OpeningHours/{start}/{end}/.

offset.description: Skip this many items (default 0). Pass the previous reply's next_offset.

limit.description: Items to return, 1-1000 (default 200). The reply's next_offset says where to continue.

tools.name: tamigo_register_attendance
tools.title: Register check-ins / check-outs
tools.description: WRITE: register check-in and check-out times in the Tamigo timesheet, for one or many employees (the same call a POS system makes). Each entry names a department key and an employee key (the POS keys set in Tamigo under Configuration -> Departments / POS Keys; they are shown by tamigo_list_departments and tamigo_list_employees) and EITHER a check_in_time OR a check_out_time, in chronological order per employee. A break is registered by giving the same activity_name (for example Lunch, SmallBreak) on its check-in and its check-out. Tamigo may round the times by the company's rules, and the reply echoes the times actually registered. This changes worked hours and wages: it is not undone by repeating it, so confirm the entries first.

check_in_time.description: Local date-time without a timezone, yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss (the workplace's local time).

check_out_time.description: Local date-time without a timezone, yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss (the workplace's local time).

activity_name.description: Optional break/activity name, e.g. Lunch or SmallBreak.

tools.name: tamigo_upload_daily_revenue
tools.title: Upload daily revenue
tools.description: WRITE: import daily revenue per department into Tamigo (the same call a cash-register system makes), used for revenue-based planning and KPIs. Each row is a department key (the POS key set in Tamigo), a date and a revenue amount (a plain number with a dot as decimal separator). A date that already has revenue for that department may be overwritten by Tamigo, so confirm the rows first. POST /Revenues/.
